en.q: What compositing technique films against a solid-color background (like green screen) and later replaces it with different footage?
en.e: Extracts and makes a specific color transparent so it can be composited with a new background.

en.q: What is the process of adjusting a video's color, tone, and contrast to match the final creative intent called?
en.e: The creative color-adjustment stage used to establish the overall mood of a piece.

en.q: What early stage of color correction matches out lighting and exposure inconsistencies from shooting?
en.e: The foundational adjustment, before grading, that evens out color and brightness variation between shots.

en.q: What transition effect gradually fades out one shot while the next shot fades in?
en.e: Often used to softly convey the passage of time or a scene change.

en.q: What transition effect switches to the next shot by wiping across the frame in a set direction?
en.e: A transition where new footage enters from one direction while part of the old frame remains briefly.

en.q: What is the image, holding transparency information as grayscale values, used to separate a subject from the background for compositing called?
en.e: Controls which areas are shown or hidden — typically white shows, black hides.

en.q: What technology analyzes specific motion in live-action footage so CG elements can accurately follow it?
en.e: Analyzes camera shake or subject motion so CG elements can blend seamlessly with live action.

en.q: What code, assigned to each frame of a video, indicates its position in time?
en.e: Uniquely identifies playback position in a hours:minutes:seconds:frames format.

en.q: What unit expresses the number of still images (frames) displayed per second?
en.e: Higher values produce smoother motion, but also increase data size.

en.q: What is the general term for the methods and standards used to compress and decompress video data?
en.e: A blend of "coder" and "decoder"; H.264 is a well-known example.

en.q: What file format (such as MP4 or MOV) bundles video, audio, and metadata together?
en.e: Acts as a "box" that packages video, audio, subtitles, and more into a single file.

en.q: In editing software, what is the workspace where clips and effects are arranged along a time axis called?
en.e: The central workspace where material is arranged on multiple tracks over time for editing.

en.q: What kind of shot is filmed continuously for a long duration without any cuts or change of viewpoint?
en.e: Sustains tension or a sense of realism by avoiding cuts entirely.

en.q: What editing technique creates a jarring effect by cutting together shots from the same angle without continuous time flow?
en.e: Deliberately creates a discontinuous feel to compress time or convey speed.

en.q: What editing technique has the audio from one shot continue before or after the corresponding video cut?
en.e: Offsets the timing of audio and video cuts to create smoother, more natural scene transitions.

en.q: What kind of cut is inserted to explain a situation, showing a close-up of an object or detail?
en.e: A close-up of hands or a prop, inserted to add context to a scene.

en.q: What is the base shot that covers an entire scene from one angle, used as an editing foundation, called?
en.e: The reference wide shot other shots are cut against during editing.

en.q: What is the shot showing another character's expression or response to a speaker called?
en.e: Used in dialogue scenes to show the listener's response.

en.q: What wide shot, shown early on to explain a scene's location or situation, is called?
en.e: A wide shot, like a building exterior, used to set up a scene's setting first.

en.q: What element overlays subtitle or caption text on top of a video?
en.e: A text element shown over a video, such as a person's name or an explanation.

en.q: What term expresses the amount of data used per unit of time in video editing?
en.e: A higher value tends to produce higher quality, but also increases data size.

en.q: What is the final stage of editing, where all elements are integrated and the completed data is locked, called?
en.e: The stage where all editing and revisions are finished and the final deliverable is locked.

en.q: What is the work of combining sound effects, music, and dialogue into a finished audio mix called?
en.e: Work that balances the volume and placement of multiple audio tracks into a finished mix.

en.q: What is the moment of switching from one shot to another itself called, in video editing?
en.e: The most basic kind of transition, where one shot instantly switches to the next.

en.q: What editing technique rhythmically connects several short shots to convey the passage of time or an emotional shift?
en.e: Connects a series of short shots together to compress time or build emotional intensity.

en.q: Which of the following has little direct relevance to a final export checklist in editing?
en.e: Revisiting the storyboard is a planning-stage task, not part of a final export checklist.

en.q: In editing software, what mechanism stacks multiple video tracks so an upper track covers the one below it?
en.e: Multiple tracks are stacked, with upper tracks visually covering the lower ones during composite.

en.q: What should a compositor check to blend live-action and CG elements together convincingly?
c: Matching light direction, color, and grain/noise
en.e: Blending live-action and CG naturally requires matching light direction, color tone, and grain.

en.q: What is the work of converting a finished video into its final format for distribution or screening called?
en.e: Converts edited data into a video file format suited to distribution or screening.

en.q: In editing a dialogue scene, what is the main effect of cutting to the other person's reaction while the speaker is still talking?
c: Showing the listener's response conveys conversational rhythm and emotional nuance
It allows copyright notices to be omitted
en.e: Inserting a reaction shot conveys emotion and timing that dialogue alone can't fully carry.

en.q: What is the general term for the rights automatically granted to the creator of a copyrighted work?
en.e: Arises automatically upon creation, without any registration requirement.

en.q: Which part of copyright covers the economic right to authorize reproduction, screening, and public transmission of a work?
en.e: The economic rights, which can be transferred or licensed to others.

en.q: Which part of copyright protects an author's honor and intentions, and cannot be transferred?
en.e: Rights that remain personally with the author and cannot be assigned to others.

en.q: Which right is NOT included among an author's moral rights?
en.e: The right of reproduction belongs to the economic rights, not the moral rights.

en.q: What right protects the economic value of an individual's name and likeness?
en.e: Restricts unauthorized commercial use of a well-known person's name or image, such as in advertising.

en.q: What framework displays standardized license terms for using a work, bridging rights holders and users?
en.e: An international system combining terms like attribution, non-commercial use, and no-derivatives to state usage conditions clearly.

en.q: What right protects marks or names used to distinguish goods or services?
en.e: Protects logos, brand names, and other identifiers of origin.

en.q: What right protects the design of an article (its shape, pattern, color, etc.)?
en.e: A registration-based right protecting the external appearance of industrial products.

en.q: Which intellectual property right protects inventions?
en.e: A registration-based right protecting technical ideas that are novel and involve an inventive step.

en.q: What is a newly created work called when made by translating, arranging, or transforming an existing work?
en.e: A new work created with the original rights holder's permission.

en.q: What system generally makes a company the author of works created by employees in the course of their duties?
en.e: Under certain conditions, the legal entity — not the individual employee who created it — becomes the author.

en.q: In Japan, how long does copyright protection generally last after the author's death (following the 2018 law revision)?
en.e: Extended from the previous 50 years to 70 years under legislation implementing the TPP agreement.

en.q: What is it called when a work is used without the rights holder's explicit permission?
en.e: A general term for any act that violates a copyright holder's rights.

en.q: Under Japanese copyright law, what system allows using a work without the copyright holder's permission if conditions like crediting the source are met?
en.e: Japan's "citation" provision sets specific, defined requirements distinct from the U.S. concept of fair use.

en.q: Who is protected by "neighboring rights" (rights related to copyright)?
c: Performers, record producers, broadcasters, and similar parties
Only the creator of the work itself
en.e: Granted not to the original creator of a work, but to those who contribute to conveying it to the public.

en.q: What is needed when a production uses a photo asset shot by someone else?
en.e: Using a third party's copyrighted work requires checking its license terms.

en.q: What is a work called once its copyright term has expired and it is free for anyone to use?
en.e: Refers to a work whose rights have lapsed, allowing free use without permission.

en.q: When no special terms are specified in a contract, what is generally true about who owns the copyright of CG work created for a client?
c: It depends on the contract terms — it isn't automatically the client's
It always automatically belongs to the client
It always automatically belongs to the creator and cannot change
No concept of copyright applies at all
en.e: Copyright ownership depends on the contract, so it should be clearly defined in a commission agreement.

en.q: What is the fee a user pays to a rights holder in exchange for permission to use a copyrighted work called?
en.e: The payment made to a rights holder in exchange for permission to use a work.

en.q: What document, shown on asset-distribution sites, sets the conditions and scope of use for a work?
en.e: A document defining whether commercial use is allowed, credit requirements, and other usage conditions.

en.q: What is a main effect gained by registering a trademark?
c: Exclusive use of the name or logo within the registered category of goods/services
Automatic acquisition of copyright over a work
Exclusive right to practice an invention
en.e: Grants the right to exclude others from using an identical or similar mark within the registered category.

en.q: What is it called when fans create new original works based on an existing character?
en.e: An activity often carried out within official guidelines, since the original work's copyright still applies.

en.q: What is a work created jointly by multiple people, whose individual contributions cannot be separated and used individually, called?
en.e: A work created jointly by multiple authors whose individual contributions cannot be separated.

en.q: What right prohibits altering a work against the author's wishes, preserving its integrity?
en.e: One of the moral rights of the author, protecting a work from unwanted alteration.

en.q: What right lets an author decide whether and when to make a work public?
en.e: Protects an unpublished work from being made public against the author's wishes.

en.q: What right lets an author decide whether and how their name is displayed on a work?
en.e: The right to decide how the author's name is shown — real name, anonymous, or pen name.

en.q: What should be specifically checked before commercially using an image created with generative AI?
c: The terms of service and rights of the service used
en.e: Copyright and commercial-use terms differ between generative AI services, so checking them in advance is necessary.

en.q: Under what condition is crediting required when using a free asset someone else has published?
c: When the asset's license terms require a credit
en.e: Whether a credit is required depends on the license terms attached to each asset.

en.q: What right is granted to performers, record producers, and broadcasters — those who help convey a work — rather than to its original creator?
en.e: Granted not to a work's original creator, but to those who contribute to conveying it to the public.

en.q: If a contract for delivered CG work does not specify who owns the copyright, what is the most appropriate action to take?
c: Confirm and agree copyright ownership with the client again, in writing
Do nothing and leave it to custom
Assume the copyright has been waived
Assume no concept of copyright applies at all
en.e: Leaving ownership unclear invites disputes, so it should be clarified in writing between the contracting parties.
